evidence: The X-ray spectra of Zn(O,S) films with different values of the S/(S þO) ratio. ZnO has a polycrystalline structure with {100} (2 θ¼31.9°) and {002} (2 θ¼ 34.4°) as main crystallographic orientations, according to what reported earlier for ZnO films deposited by S-ALD. The XRD spectrum of Zn(O,S) with S/(SþO)¼0.17 presents still the {100} and {002} crystallographic peaks of the ZnO film. The shift of the peaks towards lower angles suggests that the incorporation of S in the ZnO lattice induces a tensile stress in the layer, due to the shorter ionic radius of S (26 – 51 pm) as compared to O (124 – 128 pm). When the S/(S þ O) ratio is increased from 0.31 to 0.72, the films become amorphous due to the lattice mismatch between the hexagonal wurtzite structure of ZnO and the cubic zinc blende lattice of ZnS.
